description: End-to-end notification pipeline: send → dispatch → workers → event-writer. Every panel here is backed by an instrument that exists; see docs/observability/metrics-reference.md.

panels.title: Pipeline throughput per minute
panels.description: The four stages of one notification's life. accepted counts requests, the rest count per notification per channel, so dispatched >= accepted whenever fan-out is working. A gap opening between dispatched and delivered is the pipeline falling behind or failing.

panels.title: Per-channel delivery failure ratio
panels.description: Failed terminal outcomes as a share of all terminal outcomes, by channel. Terminal means retries are already spent, so a flaky provider that eventually succeeds does not appear here. This is what HermesDeliveryFailureRate alerts on.

panels.title: Dispatch template cache hit rate
panels.description: Hits as a share of all template cache consultations. A ratio near zero means dispatch is doing a template SELECT per notification — correct, but not what the cache is for. Check the result=error series if this drops suddenly.

panels.title: Provider call latency p95
panels.description: Time in the provider call alone, split by channel and provider — the part of a delivery Hermes does not control. Compare against the consumer's AckWait: a p95 approaching it means JetStream is redelivering messages whose handlers are still running.

panels.title: Where notifications are lost
panels.description: Everything left of a delivery attempt. Drops are the routing rules declining to deliver — a steady background of no_contact is normal, a step change is a template or preference regression. Dispatch failures and publish rejections are the opposite: nothing declined, the notification was lost anyway, so any nonzero rate is a defect.

panels.title: Event writer batches
panels.description: The end of the pipeline. Flush rate pinned near 2/s per replica means every flush is a timer flush and the batcher is idle; batch size hugging 100 means size is the trigger, which is the healthy shape under load. Dropped events are unrecoverable — the messages were acked before batching.

panels.title: Synthetic probe end-to-end latency
panels.description: The prober's own verdict on send → websocket. The only panel here that measures notifications arriving rather than a proxy for it.
